summary: At Alabama, keep the offense flexible and make the defense fit the run without losing its eyes in coverage. A back releasing into space can offer the safe throw when pressure arrives.

items.headline: Smart flags run-defense problems against Vanderbilt’s unusual looks
items.tldr: Monday’s comments put both scheme and execution under review. Watch the first step and the gap responsibility before judging the final tackle.

items.headline: Phillips caught five passes for 75 yards against Vanderbilt
items.tldr: His work as a receiving back offers another way to keep a possession moving. Watch the outlet when downfield coverage holds.

items.headline: Georgia’s offensive line has kept the same starters throughout the season
items.tldr: That continuity is a starting point, not a promise about Saturday’s lineup. Watch communication when Alabama changes the pressure picture.

items.headline: Alabama’s Griffin posted nine tackles and a sack off the bench
items.tldr: The opponent’s depth matters when the personnel changes. Watch the protection identify the active pressure threat rather than relying on the first lineup.

items.headline: Alabama is monitoring the weather; no game change is announced
items.tldr: The school says it currently has no plans to alter Saturday’s Georgia game. Check official updates before traveling; a possible change is not a confirmed postponement.

lead.headline: Keep the eyes right.
lead.body: Read the block before chasing the ball. On offense, use the available outlet and keep the quarterback’s next decision manageable.
